Nicolas of Antioch
NIK-o-las
proper noun
From the Greek Nikolaos, “conqueror of the people,” a proselyte of Antioch chosen among the seven to serve tables.

📖 Biblical Definition

Nicolas was a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven men chosen by the church at Jerusalem to serve tables, when the daily ministration to the widows had been neglected and the apostles would not leave the word of God to serve tables (Act 6:2). The multitude chose seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, and among them Stephen and Philip and the rest, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch (Act 6:5). These the apostles set apart with prayer and the laying on of hands, that they might oversee the temporal care of the saints while the apostles gave themselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word (Act 6:4). The dictionary marks Nicolas among the first servants, or deacons, of the church, and notes that he was a proselyte, a Gentile who had been brought to the God of Israel and then to Christ, a sign of the gospel reaching beyond the natural seed of Abraham. His appointment, with the rest, teaches the church to order her mercy-ministry under godly men of honest report, that the word may not be hindered and the needy not neglected. The choosing of the seven, and the office it founded, is honoured of the dictionary as the New Testament pattern for the deacon, that all things be done decently and in order (1Co 14:40), and that the saints be served in body while the ministers serve them in the word.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven chosen to serve tables in the early church at Jerusalem.

expand to see more

NICOLAS OF ANTIOCH, a proselyte of Antioch among the seven chosen to serve tables.

He was set apart when the widows were neglected in the daily ministration.

He was one of seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom.

The apostles set them apart with prayer and laying on of hands.

A later tradition linking him to the Nicolaitanes is uncertain.

📖 Key Scripture

Act 6:5 — "And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch:"

Act 6:3 — "Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business."

Act 6:4 — "But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word."

1Co 14:40 — "Let all things be done decently and in order."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture; Nicolas witnesses to the founding of the deacon’s office for the ordered care of the saints.

expand to see more

Nicolas has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as one of the seven first servants of the church. A tradition of later times would link his name to the Nicolaitanes whose deeds the Lord hated (Rev 2:6, 15); but the Scripture makes no such charge, and the connection is uncertain and not to be pressed against a man whom the church chose as of honest report.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the godly ordering of the church’s mercy-ministry, that the needy be served and the word not hindered. The seven, Nicolas among them, were chosen as men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, and set apart with prayer and the laying on of hands; so the office of the deacon was founded for the temporal care of the saints while the elders give themselves to prayer and the word. That Nicolas was a proselyte witnesses to the gospel reaching beyond the natural seed of Abraham; and the dictionary honours the decent and orderly governing of the household of God, where all things are done decently and in order.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “conqueror of the people,” Nicolas names a proselyte chosen among the seven.

Nicolas of Antioch — Greek Nikolaos, “conqueror of the people.”

He was a proselyte of Antioch, a Gentile brought to the faith.

He was one of the seven chosen to serve tables.

He was a man of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost.

A later tradition linking him to the Nicolaitanes is uncertain.

Usage

"Like Nicolas among the seven, godly men serve the saints that the word be not hindered."

"Look ye out seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom."

"Let all things be done decently and in order in the house of God."
